title: New treatment
description: Reports of a controversial new treatment at the hospital

pitches.title: Second Opinion
pitches.text: Patients recover overnight, but their reflections still limp and bleed. The team follows the discarded symptoms into the hospital mirrors and finds a physician from a reversed world trading healthy bodies for sick counterparts. When the mirrors begin exporting an epidemic, the investigators persuade both doctors to exchange medical knowledge instead of patients, then smash the transfer mirror; their own bruises remain depressingly uninsured.

pitches.title: Borrowed Tomorrow
pitches.text: A rejuvenation ward sends elderly patients home young, while nearby children develop arthritis. Birth records reveal that the treatment borrows health from each patient's youngest relative, and the inventor insists this counts as family care. The team reverses the flow during a promotional demonstration, restoring the children and aging the inventor by every year he stole; he survives, demanding a senior discount on his arrest transport.

pitches.title: The Pain Ward
pitches.text: An experimental anesthetic eliminates pain, but patients return because something is stalking them. Empty beds acquire bruises matching theirs, leading the investigators to a creature assembled from severed pain, desperate to return to its owners. They reunite patients with their accumulated suffering in supervised small doses, dissolving the creature; the hospital cancels the breakthrough and advertises the same program as unusually honest physical therapy.

pitches.title: A Better Bedside Manner
pitches.text: Patients praise a new therapist while gradually forgetting everyone except her. Interviews expose identical memories of a childhood friendship that never happened: the therapist is a lonely psychic parasite implanting herself into every meaningful relationship. The team offers her a real friendship, then forces her to relinquish the stolen ones before she erases the town's families; their mandatory weekly tea appointment becomes the case's least reimbursable expense.

pitches.title: Ghost Graft
pitches.text: A surgeon repairs damaged organs using translucent tissue, and recipients start craving the dead donors' unfinished errands. The investigators discover donated ghosts trapped inside the grafts, with one furious gangster organizing a mass bodily takeover. They locate the donors' actual unfinished business and negotiate releases before surgery, leaving stable empty scaffolds behind; the gangster settles for having his dreadful unpublished poetry mailed to his widow.

pitches.title: Discharge Into Yesterday
pitches.text: Cured patients vanish from the records, although relatives remember visiting them. The ward's new scanner sends people backward to the day before their illnesses began, where prevention rewrites their lives and starts erasing the hospital itself. The team enters yesterday with a mundane diagnosis to anchor the building, returns the missing patients, and destroys the scanner; the miraculous prevention program ends with everyone still needing ordinary follow-up care.

pitches.title: Good Bacteria
pitches.text: A probiotic treatment works so well that patients grow matching moss and gather on the roof at dawn. The team traces the culture to an intelligent extraterrestrial ecosystem trying to turn its grateful hosts into a walking forest. Rather than burn the patients, they move the colony into the hospital's neglected rooftop garden and make its survival contingent on voluntary donations; it becomes a furious but effective groundskeeper.

pitches.title: The Cure Wants Credit
pitches.text: A new cancer therapy produces impossible recoveries followed by patients speaking in an ancient god's voice. Old surgical notes reveal a healing deity bottled as a drug, waking as enough of it accumulates in human bodies. The investigators stage a public acknowledgment of the captive god and release its remaining substance into a shrine; it preserves existing cures but refuses further service until the hospital stops charging for miracles it stole.

pitches.title: Stay Positive
pitches.text: A wellness wing cures depression by physically removing patients' despair, leaving them recklessly cheerful while black rain falls over its neighbors. The removed emotions have pooled into a storm that will drown the town in other people's grief. Investigators help patients reclaim the feelings alongside genuine support, weakening the storm; its last thunderclap destroys the wellness billboard proclaiming that happiness is a choice, improving several locals' moods immediately.

pitches.title: The Visitor
pitches.text: The hospital's miracle treatment is simply allowing a small silent child to sit beside patients, who recover as staff become exhausted. The team finds the child is Death's replacement, granting reprieves by spending nurses' lifespans because nobody taught it the consequences. They reunite it with its missing predecessor, who honors the completed reprieves and restores the stolen years; Death leaves the team a thank-you basket containing entirely unsuitable fruit.

title: Reformed prisoners
description: Prisoners leaving the local jail are perhaps too reformed

pitches.title: The Confession Diet
pitches.text: Released prisoners apologize for crimes they never committed, and actual offenders begin sleeping soundly. Investigators trace a chaplain who feeds a penitent demon with borrowed guilt, making his congregation scapegoats for the whole town. They force the demon to hear confessions from the genuine perpetrators and release its original hosts; the warden loses his perfect rehabilitation figures, while the town discovers how many respectable people urgently need lawyers.

pitches.title: Better Halves
pitches.text: Every released inmate is polite, punctual, and terrified of their own shadow. The jail's psychologist has split each personality, imprisoning unwanted impulses in a cellar where the shadows are combining into a brutal escape artist. The team reunites prisoners with their rejected traits before the composite reaches daylight; rehabilitation becomes slower and less photogenic, and one restored man celebrates by finally telling his parole officer that his jokes are bad.

pitches.title: Saints on Probation
pitches.text: Former inmates perform miracles and voluntarily sweep sidewalks until they collapse. A relic in the chapel has replaced their souls with exhausted saints, while the prisoners' souls remain trapped inside a vending machine demanding change. The investigators break the relic's hold with the saints' own insistence that goodness must be voluntary, restoring everyone; one saint stays briefly to expose the cafeteria as the jail's most unforgivable crime.

pitches.title: The Quiet Sentence
pitches.text: Released prisoners never complain, even while being exploited by employers. Observing their synchronized flinches, the team discovers invisible jailers following them home and punishing every forbidden thought. The jailers are manifestations of a judge's lifelong desire for absolute obedience, anchored to his unwritten sentences. Investigators get the judge to experience his own supervision, making him revoke the sentences; the freed prisoners immediately form an extremely noisy tenants' association.

pitches.title: Too Good to Be Human
pitches.text: Former prisoners rescue kittens but forget how to eat and recognize their families. A rehabilitation contractor is replacing them with benevolent clay replicas, storing the originals as supposedly unrecoverable raw material. The replicas assist the investigation after learning the truth, rescuing the originals and refusing dissolution. The town gets both its missing residents and a new population of ethical duplicates, while the contractor's promise to halve incarceration costs proves mathematically disastrous.

pitches.title: Time Served
pitches.text: People jailed overnight emerge repentant and fluent in extinct languages. A broken cell door opens into a millennium-long exile where inmates found civilizations before returning moments later. When that civilization sends an army through to rescue its missing monarchs, the team reveals the involuntary sentences and brokers permanent closure of the doorway. The veterans remain free, though explaining twelve former spouses to their current partners takes considerably longer than booking.

pitches.title: The Nice Gang
pitches.text: Released criminals become compulsively generous, giving away furniture and blood. Their tattoos are sprouting identical flowers: a prison gardening project exposed them to a compassion fungus that will consume hosts once nothing remains to donate. The investigators exploit its hunger by offering a self-renewing compost heap, drawing it out alive. The prisoners keep their memories of empathy but regain boundaries, beginning with declining another unpaid interview about the program's success.

pitches.title: Tomorrow's Regret
pitches.text: Inmates leave trembling and immediately prevent accidents that have not happened. A medium running counseling sessions shows each prisoner the harm of their future choices, but a manipulative future ghost selects visions to ensure its own birth. Comparing contradictory predictions exposes the fraud; the team encourages one small harmless rebellion that breaks the ghost's necessary chain of events. Prisoners retain real lessons while the erased manipulator never becomes anybody's problem.

pitches.title: The Warden's Children
pitches.text: Everyone released suddenly calls the warden Dad and defends him despite remembering abuse. Investigators find his dead daughter's imaginary family living inside a dollhouse, reshaping prisoners into siblings so she never has to grieve again. They let her confront the real man's failings rather than attack her home, breaking her fantasy's grip. She departs with her actual memories, the prisoners recover, and the warden finds paternal immunity absent from criminal law.

pitches.title: A Model Community
pitches.text: Former inmates return to jail voluntarily each evening, insisting freedom is dangerously inefficient. The jail was built over an insect queen's buried nest, and its pheromones are recruiting humans into a perfect obedient colony. The team finds her dying larvae beneath the exercise yard and relocates the surviving nest, ending the influence without extermination. The prisoners remain friends but abandon communal living after discovering the queen expected everyone to work for food alone.

title: Interrupted construction
description: A construction project has dug up something strange

pitches.title: The Town Beneath
pitches.text: Workers uncover a tiny inhabited town whose residents insist the surface city is their ceiling. Excavation damages its sky, and miniature storms begin appearing above the construction site as scale reverses. Survey maps show both towns occupy the same space at different magnifications. Investigators repair the buried weather tower and divert the foundations around it; the developer must redesign the luxury complex to accommodate several thousand unexpectedly well-organized downstairs neighbors.

pitches.title: An Unfinished Burial
pitches.text: An excavator finds a giant hand gripping a wedding ring, and the ground starts following a heartbeat. The buried giant was murdered before reaching his bride, whose fossilized body lies across the river. Investigators reunite the ring with her remains, allowing both to settle into ordinary geology instead of waking beneath town. Construction resumes until someone asks whether building condos across a reconciled couple constitutes desecration or merely a very poor bedroom layout.

pitches.title: Foundations of Nothing
pitches.text: Workers uncover a perfectly smooth black void that swallows rubble but returns objects nobody remembers owning. The team discovers it contains demolished possibilities: buildings the town planned but never built, now trying to become real simultaneously. They find the oldest abandoned plan, a public shelter, and build it at the opening, giving the void one agreed future. The luxury developer is furious that saving reality has also produced affordable housing.

pitches.title: The Root Problem
pitches.text: A foundation dig exposes a beating wooden heart, and nearby houses sprout roots that drag them toward the site. It belongs to the ancient forest cleared for the town, rebuilding itself from the wood inside residents' homes. The investigators locate its last living seedling and transplant the heart there before neighborhoods collapse. The revived forest accepts a protected plot; residents keep their houses but must apologize to their increasingly judgmental dining tables.

pitches.title: Bomb Shelter Guests
pitches.text: Construction opens a sealed shelter full of people calmly awaiting an apocalypse that already happened outside their time bubble. The moment its clock restarts, their predicted catastrophe begins manifesting around the excavation. The team discovers the prediction was generated by the shelter itself to justify remaining sealed. They dismantle its forecasting core while evacuating residents, preventing the disaster; the survivors are relieved until they learn the price of groceries since 1962.

pitches.title: The Sleeping Road
pitches.text: An uncovered stretch of ancient pavement keeps extending overnight, and anyone walking it arrives at places they regret leaving. The road is a migratory spirit trapped under modern asphalt, trying to reconnect its scattered travelers before dying. Investigators guide a final procession of willing residents, then let it end at the coast. It becomes ordinary stone; several people return reconciled, while one investigator's lost luggage arrives with a profoundly obsolete compensation voucher.

pitches.title: Hard Hat Egg
pitches.text: Workers mistake a huge translucent egg for a buried fuel tank, then hear familiar voices from inside. Its embryo copies anyone nearby to assemble a convincing human identity, and hatching will erase whichever person it chooses to impersonate. The team persuades it to invent someone new instead, contributing contradictory autobiographies until no original matches. It emerges as a harmless stranger with six birthdays and immediately complains that nobody has offered it a paid apprenticeship.

pitches.title: A Door Without a House
pitches.text: An excavated door opens onto the same site decades ahead, where an investigator's statue honors their death preventing a collapse. Future records show that warning the developer creates the shortcut that causes that collapse. The team breaks the loop by demolishing the doorway and publicly exposing the shortcut before construction continues. The statue disappears, but its dedication plaque survives as excellent evidence that the agency has technically won at least one lifetime achievement award.

pitches.title: The Old Water Main
pitches.text: Workers uncover pipes pumping seawater uphill, although the coast is hundreds of miles away. As sea creatures appear in toilets, investigators learn the pipes are veins of a buried ocean spirit whose body was stranded when continents moved. They use an abandoned canal to restore its connection to the real sea, allowing it to depart without drowning town. The city bills them for unauthorized plumbing despite the measurable disappearance of bathroom sharks.

pitches.title: The First Brick
pitches.text: A crew finds a brick inscribed with every resident's name, including people born that morning. It is the town's supernatural foundation; removing it lets neighborhoods vanish when nobody watches. Historical records reveal the founder stole it from a wandering settlement, trapping its inhabitants inside the brick. The investigators release those ghosts and convince current residents to collectively claim their homes, establishing a new foundation through belonging; the developer complains that community sentiment is not load-bearing.

title: Escaped experiment
description: A lab is requesting help retrieving an escaped specimen

pitches.title: The Escape Is a Rescue
pitches.text: A lab asks the team to capture a shapeless specimen stealing pet carriers. Its trail leads to other test animals, which it absorbs unharmed to carry them out of captivity. The creature is a collective shelter intelligence born from the animals' shared fear, and pursuing it makes it expand toward the zoo. The investigators expose the experiments and arrange genuine sanctuary, letting its passengers leave; the lab invoices them for returning the specimen substantially smaller.

pitches.title: The Missing Tomorrow
pitches.text: The escaped specimen appears only in photographs taken tomorrow, while its victims vanish from yesterday's records. Scientists bred a predator that eats unrealized futures and have hidden its escape inside a forecast. The team draws it into a deliberately impossible future, promising a fully funded agency picnic, then destroys the machine sustaining that possibility. Everyone reappears with memories of days they never lived, and the impossible picnic remains the agency's most believable cover story.

pitches.title: Housebroken Apocalypse
pitches.text: A lab's escaped hound tears through locked doors but carefully avoids harming people. Each destruction stops a later catastrophe, revealing it senses disasters and was confined because its forecasts disrupted profitable research. The scientists' planned recapture will trigger a reactor failure the animal has been trying to reach. Investigators help it break the reactor safely, then find it a willing home; its new owner accepts that good behavior occasionally requires demolishing the kitchen.

pitches.title: The Specimen Has a Job
pitches.text: The lab wants its escaped mimic returned, but every witness remembers a different helpful stranger. Tracking unexplained completed chores reveals it survived by becoming whoever people needed, until conflicting identities begin tearing it apart. The team finds it working five minimum-wage jobs to buy its freedom and helps it choose a single self rather than surrender. Its new permanent face is its own invention; the researchers mourn losing their perfect unpaid research assistant.

pitches.title: A Thought on the Loose
pitches.text: No one can describe the escaped specimen without immediately forgetting why they entered the room. The lab cultured a living distraction that travels between interrupted thoughts, and it is multiplying through emergency calls. Investigators bait it with an unfinished crossword inside a sealed neural recording, then complete the puzzle to trap it in a final answer. The dangerous thought becomes inert ink, while the lab's spokesperson insists memory loss was never an officially approved side effect.

pitches.title: The Warmest Place
pitches.text: An escaped glowing embryo nests in boilers, sending temperatures up while its pursuers demand a rapid return. Lab logs reveal it is a baby star that will ignite soon, and containment was never possible beyond the grant demonstration. With no extraction team coming, investigators use the lab's original summoning dish to return it to its cold celestial nursery. It lights up safely overhead, leaving the town with a new constellation shaped like a distinctly unflattering resignation letter.

pitches.title: The Experiment Escaped Last Year
pitches.text: The lab's search starts pointing to a respected local teacher who remembers growing up in town. Its specimen escaped as a child and rewrote surrounding memories to give itself a childhood; the frantic retrieval order was delayed for twelve years inside its protective illusion. Investigators find genuine relationships beneath the invented history and stop a forced extraction that would erase the teacher's students. The creature relinquishes its false credentials and stays, enrolling in teacher training amid considerable paperwork.

pitches.title: Negative Animal
pitches.text: The escaped creature leaves footprints made of missing pavement and eats the color out of gardens. It was grown in a universe of antimatter meanings, where human attention hurts it and invisibility is starvation. Investigators follow its trail to a ruined darkroom, where it has painstakingly assembled a doorway home from photographic negatives. They finish the doorway before the lab's floodlights kill it; restored color returns in one spectacular burst, briefly making everyone's tax documents fluorescent.

pitches.title: The Carrier
pitches.text: The specimen is an ordinary rat carrying an immortal human mind who broadcasts desperate pleas through nearby radios. His supposed recovery team intends to harvest other minds once he proves survival outside a body. Investigators find the original volunteer consent concealed in the lab's records, rescue the remaining subjects, and return him to his preserved body. He survives with an enduring cheese preference and sues for wages covering eight months spent testing mazes after the experiment's official completion.

pitches.title: Capture the Hunter
pitches.text: The specimen's route is littered with emptied protective cages, but no human casualties. Investigators discover it is a parasitic predator released accidentally while scientists tried to contain the far larger creature now hunting it across town. Rather than return either monster to an inadequate lab, they lure the hunter into the specimen's abandoned habitat and send both through their origin portal. The lab calls the elimination of two existential threats a disappointing failure to preserve valuable research assets.

title: Noisy neighbor
description: Strange noises are coming from a neighbor's house

pitches.title: The Baby Upstairs
pitches.text: A neighbor's endless crying makes walls sweat and adults age overnight. The team discovers an elderly widow accidentally summoned her unborn child's ghost, which has been waiting decades to grow up and is borrowing time from surrounding households. They help her acknowledge the life she actually lived instead of the one she lost, allowing the child to depart. Stolen years return; the widow keeps one harmless laugh recorded on a phone she still cannot operate.

pitches.title: Renovating the Afterlife
pitches.text: Drilling continues from an empty house whose rooms keep changing dimensions. A dead handyman is repairing a hole between worlds, but his living client refuses to approve the work because completion would confirm her husband's death. Investigators follow construction marks into the leaking afterlife and reunite the couple for a final goodbye. The handyman closes the breach and finally leaves, pausing only to explain that emotional closure does not excuse ignoring the agreed deposit.

pitches.title: The House Practices
pitches.text: Neighbors hear footsteps and conversations that precisely predict tomorrow's arguments. The house is rehearsing its inhabitants' future because a subterranean predator hunts noisy outcomes; soon it plans to silence every resident permanently to keep them safe. Investigators discover a previous owner's acoustic experiments and move the predator toward recordings played in an abandoned quarry. The grateful house stops rehearsing, though it retains an annoying habit of warning guests before they spill red wine.

pitches.title: A Very Small War
pitches.text: Nightly explosions come from a quiet pensioner's model railway, whose tiny soldiers are crossing into the kitchen. He collected battlefield soil that contains a century-old territorial dispute, and the miniature armies mistake his full-sized neighbors for invading giants. The team locates the soldiers' surviving descendants and arranges a peace treaty acknowledging both sides' dead. The war ends, leaving a functioning model town whose residents demand that the pensioner stop rerouting their trains whenever he gets bored.

pitches.title: The Dinner Guest
pitches.text: A neighbor's dining room emits chewing loud enough to rattle windows, and deliveries disappear at the doorstep. An unemployed cook invited an ancient hunger spirit to critique dinner, then kept feeding it because admitting failure meant it would eat her. The team identifies its lost appetite as grief rather than hunger and serves a reconstruction of its mother's last meal. Satisfied at last, it leaves, granting the cook one honest compliment and absolutely no tip.

pitches.title: Duet Through the Wall
pitches.text: A singer practicing at home harmonizes with voices that make listeners forget their names. The duet partner is a drowned river spirit contacting her missing sister through the house's old well, and the human audience is accidentally supplying identities for its passage. Investigators trace the sister to a diverted stream and reconnect their waters, stopping the theft. The singer keeps her voice but loses her supernatural perfect pitch; she regards the restored neighbors as the case's secondary achievement.

pitches.title: The Moving Company
pitches.text: Dragging furniture is heard nightly, although the neighbor owns nothing and refuses to leave. His house is migrating sideways through parallel streets, depositing increasingly alarming alternate neighbors in the spare bedroom. Investigators discover he has been searching for a world where his wife survived, but every shift displaces someone else. He chooses the living community that keeps helping him over another search, anchoring the house; displaced visitors return home, apart from a cat that exercises its own judgment.

pitches.title: Apolite Possession
pitches.text: The noises are increasingly courteous requests to be allowed out, spoken in the voices of missing pets. A lonely collector keeps a demon sealed in an antique doll, but it has learned empathy from decades of listening to the neighborhood and wants to return the souls its former owner fed it. Investigators supervise the release and locate the pets' families; freed souls settle peacefully, and the demon departs after making the collector endure every heartfelt reunion.

pitches.title: The Night Shift
pitches.text: Machinery grinds inside a house occupied by a delivery driver who claims to sleep all night. His dreaming self runs a factory that turns neighbors' nightmares into physical products, and an unfulfilled order for a monster is assembling itself. Investigators find the dream factory and wake its workers, all unpaid echoes of exhausted locals, collapsing production. The driver loses his passive income scheme and discovers he too was paid in dream currency that cannot cover electricity.

pitches.title: Someone Under the Floor
pitches.text: Scratching beneath the neighbor's house spells out mundane shopping requests before becoming screams. Investigators find the building swallowed a burglar years ago and has been keeping him alive as a beloved parasite, refusing to lose its only resident who touched every room. They promise it regular human company and carefully extract him through the pantry. The rescued man retires from burglary, while the house becomes a community center with an exceptionally strict prohibition on locked internal doors.

title: Request from the mansion
description: Investigators requested to a prominent estate

pitches.title: The Last Heir
pitches.text: The estate's owner hires investigators because every relative who attends dinner looks progressively more like him. His ancestral portrait is copying his identity into heirs to preserve the family patriarch forever, while the current owner secretly hopes to escape. The team uncovers that the patriarch himself begged to die and his descendants misunderstood his wishes. Burning the portrait releases everyone, including the grateful owner, who immediately sells the estate and discovers nobody knows how to invoice a dead client.

pitches.title: The Grounds Have Teeth
pitches.text: Guests vanish during garden tours, and the groundskeeper refuses to trim certain hedges. The estate sits inside a sleeping creature whose landscaped organs awaken whenever the owner expands the gardens; the gardener has been quietly pruning its nerves to keep it asleep. Investigators reverse the latest excavation and coax the creature to migrate to open countryside. The mansion survives with an enormous missing basement, and its owner finally comprehends the groundskeeper's request for hazard pay.

pitches.title: The Dinner That Never Happened
pitches.text: The family wants a haunting investigated before a charity banquet, where servants keep finding place settings for people still alive but absent. Each setting belongs to someone the estate's founder ruined, and their living descendants are being summoned to inherit his unpaid moral debts. Investigators invite them openly and let them decide reparations, ending the haunting. The banquet becomes an uncomfortable restitution meeting; its wealthy host still calls it a tremendous networking opportunity.

pitches.title: The Perfect Guest
pitches.text: The estate's hostess suspects one dinner guest is an impostor, yet every guest has flawless documentation. The team discovers the mansion conjures whatever company she most wants, replacing real visitors who disappoint her with agreeable duplicates trapped in its cellar. Investigators free the originals and force her to host their uncensored anger, breaking the fantasy. Her parties become smaller and considerably livelier, while the most charming duplicate escapes to pursue a career in local politics.

pitches.title: One Room Short
pitches.text: A prominent family's mansion loses a room each night, and servants insist the house once had hundreds more. The missing rooms are payment to a passage spirit that saved the family from a historic fire, with generations expanding the house to avoid settling the debt. Investigators discover the original bargain asked only for a home, not endless tribute, and build the spirit a small permanent cottage. It returns the rooms, including a dining room full of exceptionally stale scandal.

pitches.title: A Wolf at the Lawn Party
pitches.text: The heir requests discreet help after waking muddy beside torn formalwear and fears he is a werewolf. Clues instead point to the estate's fox hunt, whose slain animals collectively possess whoever inherits the land and force them to experience the hunt from below. Investigators reconstruct the buried kill site and secure a permanent wildlife refuge. The possession ends, but the heir keeps a healthy terror of wealthy people on horseback and abandons his own expensive riding lessons.

pitches.title: The Family Silver
pitches.text: The mansion's silverware attacks guests, apparently selecting them by ancestry. It contains the souls of miners killed by the family company, and each item is hunting a descendant of its killers while the owner sells pieces to scatter the evidence. The team gathers the surviving collection and exposes the buried disaster, then establishes a memorial using reclaimed mine land. The spirits depart; the owner serves the next benefit dinner with plastic cutlery and calls it an environmental initiative.

pitches.title: The Estate Is the Client
pitches.text: The investigators arrive to discover their invitation was written by the mansion itself. Its owners are immortal squatters who keep sacrificing caretakers to maintain their youth, and the house wants someone to evict them before another worker dies. The team finds the immortality chamber and channels the stored years back into surviving victims, making the owners finally mortal. The house protects the investigators during escape, then turns itself into apartments priced low enough to offend its former residents.

pitches.title: The Undiscovered Country
pitches.text: The estate's map room shows gardens leading into countries that do not exist, and the owner's expedition has not returned. A colonial ancestor imprisoned the last fragment of a conquered dream nation in a globe; visitors now enter as its border expands into waking land. Investigators release the captive nation's ruler rather than storm its capital, recovering the expedition and stabilizing a voluntary crossing. The owner loses sovereignty over the globe and complains that the locals have abolished his admission charge.

pitches.title: The Inheritance Trial
pitches.text: The family hires help because their dying matriarch is receiving visits from younger versions of herself. Each version embodies a different life she sacrificed for the estate, and they intend to divide her descendants among incompatible realities. The team discovers she can reunite them only by relinquishing the mansion that anchored those choices. She donates it and dies whole, preserving a single world; the heirs call this a supernatural robbery and spend the wake comparing what they nearly inherited.

title: Request from the corporation
description: Investigators requested to a local office tower

pitches.title: The Floor Nobody Rents
pitches.text: Elevators deliver workers to an unlisted floor where familiar colleagues insist unfinished tasks must be completed. The tower has grown a digestive organ that feeds on unpaid overtime, retaining employees until they disappear from payroll. Investigators track its dependence on concealed working hours and make the company record and pay every shift. Without stolen time to consume, the floor collapses and releases its workers; management celebrates by commissioning an efficiency review of the rescue.

pitches.title: The Executive Weather
pitches.text: Rain falls inside the CEO's office while lower floors develop blizzards whenever quarterly results dip. He hired a weather spirit to make corporate mood literal, then trapped it in the air conditioning. As a disastrous forecast threatens to freeze the building, investigators uncover its old home beneath a demolished pond and restore a water connection. It leaves through the pipes, and the CEO learns demanding sunshine is more effective with maintenance than human resources.

pitches.title: The Company Man
pitches.text: An executive requests help after employees merge physically during brainstorming sessions. A slogan about becoming one family awakened the company's collective identity, which wants a single efficient body to execute its strategy. Investigators trace its nervous system through shared records and formally dissolve the company before the merger reaches the street. Employees separate and establish independent firms; the rescued executive asks whether everyone could keep the old brand, provoking a unanimous response.

pitches.title: An Open Position
pitches.text: Every replacement receptionist vanishes after three days. The lobby stands over an ancient crossroads where a guardian must remain awake, and an executive unknowingly dismissed the spirit who held the post. Investigators recover the former guardian from the retirement home where it took its severance, but it refuses to return. They close the crossroads by burying the lobby, recovering the missing staff and rendering the tower inaccessible; management chooses stairs through the loading dock over acknowledging a mistake.

pitches.title: The Rival in the Glass
pitches.text: Employees see rival-company staff working inside windows and begin losing hours to them. The reflective skin connects alternate corporations competing to occupy the same building, each convinced the other is a hostile acquisition. Investigators discover both originated from one founder's abandoned choice and shatter the connecting panes during the resulting boardroom invasion. The realities separate, but one investigator ends up employed by the alternate agency, whose benefits are equally imaginary and whose parking is substantially worse.

pitches.title: The Forecast Department
pitches.text: Uncanny sales predictions come true even when no customers wanted the product. A chained oracle rewrites demand, and a trainee's prediction of bankruptcy starts dissolving the tower into debt-shaped creatures. Investigators free the oracle, which can end the prophecy only by destroying the company whose fate it names. The workers escape as the tower collapses into worthless invoices; the oracle leaves, while the team discovers its rescue fee was among the first casualties.

pitches.title: A Meeting With the Departed
pitches.text: A boardroom meeting continues for days, with increasingly old-fashioned voices joining. The founder's ghost summoned every predecessor to decide whether the corporation deserves to exist, consuming living employees as testimony. Investigators bring former workers instead of executives, exposing the company's history plainly. The dead dissolve the board and release employees, leaving a viable cooperative; the founder stays to perform the entry-level work he spent his lifetime assuring people anyone could do.

pitches.title: The Office Pet
pitches.text: Staff blame a missing terrarium for coworkers developing transparent skin. Its salamander was the tower's fire spirit, secretly absorbing electrical hazards until someone took it home. Without it, the building is turning into heat that will ignite the district. Investigators restore the creature, then cut power and physically remove the accumulated hazards so it can leave. Management discovers keeping a charming mascot costs less than maintaining a safe workplace, but the mascot now knows that too.

pitches.title: Downsizing the Soul
pitches.text: Workers' badges still open doors after their holders disappear. A consulting algorithm summoned a demon that interpreted eliminating redundancy as removing everyone whose life resembles someone else's. Investigators find missing staff compressed into statistical categories in the server room and corrupt the categories using invented employee histories. People return amid the data collapse, but the company loses its actual records too; management finally has to ask its workers what they do.

pitches.title: The View From Above
pitches.text: Upper floors overlook an underwater town while those downstairs remain dry. The penthouse was raised into a drowned future by a developer inspecting tomorrow's property values, and the flood is climbing backward through the tower. Future footage identifies the flood barrier his own company will sabotage. Investigators destroy the time mechanism and expose the sabotage before it occurs, severing the future; stranded future tenants remain and demand refunds for advertised waterfront apartments.

title: Lost library
description: Investigators requested to catalog some strange books

pitches.title: Overdue Lives
pitches.text: Books contain biographies of living people, ending on the day they are cataloged. The archive belongs to Death, whose apprentice mistakes completion for a death warrant. Investigators find the apprentice's abandoned manual and deliberately catalog its own biography to demonstrate the error. Frightened by mortality, it reverses its mistaken orders and quits. Residents recover from apparent fatal accidents, while the librarian inherits an archive that now requires revising every entry until the subject actually dies.

pitches.title: The Hungry Appendix
pitches.text: Each cataloged book grows a chapter containing an investigator's private memories. A parasitic index consumes readers to make a complete account of human life, and tearing pages out scatters it into more volumes. The team traps it in a self-generating story whose ending keeps moving, then welds its book inside a steel box. The archive survives with one permanently uncataloged volume; the imprisoned index occasionally escapes as a threatening footnote in unrelated cookbooks.

pitches.title: Books for the Missing
pitches.text: Strange books describe pleasant homes in missing residents' handwriting. Investigators find a displaced neighborhood living inside escapist novels after demolition, while a collector plans to pulp the collection. They rescue the books during his attempted disposal but cannot offer the residents real housing. Some return to homelessness; others choose the fiction. The team preserves their refuge in a public reading room, whose fundraising brochure carefully avoids mentioning how much more affordable imaginary apartments are.

pitches.title: The Author's Revenge
pitches.text: Books rewrite reviewers' lives into humiliating scenes, and catalog notes become threatening dialogue. Their dead author mistakes every description for another cruel review and plans a finale killing all critics. Investigators locate his rejected manuscript and burn its final chapter, severing the revenge narrative before it reaches its conclusion. The ghost fades without reconciliation; affected reviewers recover, and the team is left wondering whether destroying someone's life's work counts as constructive criticism.

pitches.title: The Unwritten Language
pitches.text: Catalogers understand unfamiliar books but forget ordinary words afterward. The volumes preserve a dying language whose last speaker became a living dictionary and steals vocabulary to survive. Investigators locate descendants willing to learn it voluntarily, giving the language genuine speakers again. Speech returns and the dictionary releases its captives, but one investigator chooses to retain the new language at the cost of their old one; the agency adopts subtitles for staff meetings.

pitches.title: The Shelf Between Winters
pitches.text: A shelf alternates frost and flowers, returning books with messages centuries apart. It bridges a hidden world whose inhabitants seek advice to survive a failing sun, but the librarian has filed their pleas as fiction. Investigators discover instructions for the sun mechanism inside a previously untranslated volume and send them back. The world repairs its daylight and closes the bridge; the grateful recipients send a history of humanity containing several mortifying corrections.

pitches.title: The Library of Lies
pitches.text: Books cataloged as true make their contents historical fact, beginning with a local legend. They belonged to a storyteller who deliberately marked every volume fiction to preserve human freedom; rival collectors now want to rewrite ownership of town. Investigators restore the original labels, but one colleague secretly leaves a volume claiming the agency possesses a fortune. The money becomes real, along with the book's murderous source; the team returns the fortune to survive its apparent good luck.

pitches.title: The Last Reader
pitches.text: Every volume opens onto a deserted library where a figure begs catalogers to enter. It is the library's memory, pulling people into stories because its last reader died. Investigators restore its scattered collection to a public reading room, giving the consciousness a new physical home. Captive readers escape, but the library chooses to retain the dead reader's remembered presence. The living librarian accepts a ghost patron who argues about late fees with uniquely authoritative persistence.

pitches.title: Unreliable Narrators
pitches.text: Identical books give incompatible accounts of a murder, each summoning a different victim's ghost. They hold witness memories, including the killer's version where the victim deserved it. Investigators compare surviving physical evidence and publish the actual sequence, dissolving the false ghosts and freeing the original. The killer remains protected by an expired legal deadline, so the ghost spends its remaining manifestation time narrating the truth outside his very respectable office.

pitches.title: The Index of Doors
pitches.text: Books contain floor plans of vanished buildings, and opening one creates its entrance. An architect hid endangered buildings outside space, but residents have waited without daylight for decades. Investigators reopen exits before a dying book strands its occupants forever, then destroy the unstable archive after evacuating it. The missing communities return to a town that has moved on; the team receives an entire rescued office building with no utilities and an extremely real maintenance bill.

title: Estate sale
description: Investigators requested to catalog some strange artifacts

pitches.title: Everything Must Go
pitches.text: Artifacts make buyers resemble the dead collector and share his memories. He divided his soul among possessions to survive, but reassembly will overwrite the buyer owning most pieces. Investigators deliberately sell the complete collection to a mindless animated mannequin, trapping his reunited consciousness in a body that cannot leave the display stand. Buyers recover; the collector spends his immortality hearing prospective customers debate whether his nose lowers the resale value.

pitches.title: The Wrong Estate
pitches.text: Artifacts have unfamiliar uses and rooms rearrange during inventory. The sale occupies an other-dimensional home whose executor translated death as temporary relocation, selling the belongings of someone merely at work. Investigators locate the furious living owner, but buyers have already activated a domestic disposal device that is eating the street. They sacrifice the entire collection to clog it, saving town; the owner survives and gives the executor a very human performance review.

pitches.title: A Familiar Price
pitches.text: A bracelet whispers useful facts while other pieces move toward vulnerable buyers. The collector housed abandoned witch familiars in objects, and they must bond with new humans before fading. Investigators uncover the sanctuary and arrange voluntary partnerships with explicit limits. One powerful familiar refuses consent and attacks, forcing the team to destroy its vessel while saving the others; the resulting ethical adoption fair produces a remarkable argument about whether spectral snakes require pet deposits.

pitches.title: The Wedding Gifts
pitches.text: A dead couple's gifts attack anyone separating matching pieces, although some predate their birth. They reincarnated repeatedly, carrying their wedding bond into lives where one finally wanted freedom. Investigators locate her current incarnation and let her surrender the complete collection, ending the enforced bond. Her former spouse's soul loses its guaranteed route back to her and departs grieving; she celebrates an ordinary first date where no prophecy has already selected the dessert.

pitches.title: The Collector Was Collected
pitches.text: A miniature figure of the deceased changes posture overnight. He encountered beings that preserve humans as collectibles, and the sale is their cover for acquiring town. Investigators discover their handling gloves prevent miniaturization, steal them, and shrink the alien curator instead. They exchange it for every captive, recovering the owner; the departing aliens retain one authentic plastic souvenir, because nobody can endure another lecture about how hard genuine human provenance is to verify.

pitches.title: The Cabinet of Last Chances
pitches.text: Artifacts redo small regrets, but revised events strand bystanders in erased lives. A dying time traveler funds backward attempts to recover his daughter through the sales. Investigators find her alive in a reality he discarded, but recovering her would permanently erase dozens of other people. He finally chooses to stop, returning the bystanders and destroying his machines. The team preserves one impossible photograph of his daughter, refusing to describe the outcome as a successful reunification.

pitches.title: Ghosts Included
pitches.text: Every artifact has a ghost, from a murderous sword to a sulking blender. The collector rescued haunted belongings without telling heirs, and scattering them will isolate spirits who keep one another sane. Investigators establish a shared museum funded by the sale's remaining ordinary objects. The ghosts accept visitors instead of hosts, although the sword refuses peace and must remain locked away; the blender demands prominent placement in modern art and is grudgingly proven correct.

pitches.title: The Final Collection
pitches.text: Artifacts prove to be organs disguised as decorations, and the catalog resembles a dissection diagram. The dead owner was a distributed creature whose surviving organs will poison town as they decay. Investigators assemble a new body, but it awakens starving and begins swallowing the estate. They lure it into the river with the last organ and burn that organ to stop its return. The heirs inherit shed pearls and a waterfront hole where their inheritance previously stood.

pitches.title: The Thief's Conscience
pitches.text: Objects vanish from the inventory and appear at strangers' homes, dragging handlers on dangerous journeys. They remember original owners and are escaping the collector's suppressive cabinet. Investigators reconstruct acquisitions and return the stolen pieces, but one was itself stolen by its earliest remembered owner, causing an endless tug-of-war. They destroy that piece to release its captive souls; the estate's only valuable honest purchase proves to be an appalling novelty lamp.

pitches.title: Pocket Summer
pitches.text: A snow globe warms the catalog room as winter disappears and crops flower. The owner trapped an entire summer to preserve his dying spouse's final happy days, and opening it will release years of lethal heat. Investigators enter its miniature season and hear the spouse demand freedom rather than continued preservation. They break the globe underwater, boiling the estate's lake while sparing town; she departs, and the family attempts to market its loss as geothermal investment.

title: Performance enhancement
description: The high school sports team is doing unusually well

pitches.title: The Second String
pitches.text: The team never loses, but reserves weaken as stars improve. A coach's whistle transfers benchwarmers' potential to active players, and the championship will drain the reserves permanently. Investigators prove the pattern using old rosters and persuade the stars to return their stolen talent before the final. They lose honestly and save teammates; the coach demands the report still list their moral victory as an undefeated season, apparently misunderstanding both words.

pitches.title: Home Advantage
pitches.text: The team excels at home while visitors get lost in impossible stadium corridors. Its groundskeeper's ghost promised to protect children and now sees every away team as invaders. Investigators uncover his real final wish, fair chances for all, but he refuses to distinguish competition from war. They demolish the old guard booth anchoring him, ending the haunting; the rescued students plant a memorial and play the first fair match on an unusually poorly trimmed field.

pitches.title: The Last Game
pitches.text: Players use extinct formations and unfamiliar names. Commemorative uniforms host the dead championship team, seeking the game interrupted by a fatal bus crash. Investigators stage the matchup against willing descendants, allowing spirits to borrow bodies with consent. The ghosts lose but accept the completed game and depart; the modern students keep a hard-earned understanding of sportsmanship, while their coach objects that spending budget on an exhibition loss is a misuse of school funds.

pitches.title: Victory Animal
pitches.text: The new mascot inspires wins while spectators crave raw meat and players grow claws. It is fattening town on competitive aggression before consuming the crowd after the championship. Investigators find its dependence on triumph and force a public forfeit when the coach refuses. The furious crowd briefly attacks their rescuers before the starving spirit collapses into an ordinary cat. Everyone recovers; the cat refuses responsibility and scratches the principal during its first adoption interview.

pitches.title: The Scholarship Deal
pitches.text: An injured student returns unbeatable and receives letters from nonexistent universities. A recruiter from a warrior afterlife promised every player scholarships in exchange for a final victory that kills them. Investigators expose the college as an eternal battlefield, but the contract cannot be revoked without a losing championship. The team deliberately loses despite the recruiter's sabotage, escaping alive; the injured student loses his borrowed recovery and receives genuine support from teammates instead of another miracle promise.

pitches.title: Winning Backward
pitches.text: Opponents withdraw mysteriously, and players remember games nobody else played. The scoreboard lets the captain replay losses, accumulating injuries in discarded timelines where abandoned teams become a vengeful crowd. Investigators enter a replay and recover its missing versions by persuading the captain to accept one irreversible defeat. Destroying the scoreboard merges the timelines, leaving everyone alive with years of extra pain and experience; the students stop treating recovery days as personal weakness.

pitches.title: The Ideal Athlete
pitches.text: Players grow stronger and more alike, sharing one laugh. A supplement contains an organism trained to imitate the legendary champion, replacing teenagers with standardized bodies. Investigators bring the retired champion, who reveals he hated sports and wanted to dance, breaking the organism's model of perfection. It releases the hosts but retains their stolen strength as its own body, becoming a flamboyant solo dancer; the coach experiences the rescue as an incomprehensible attack on the athletic department.

pitches.title: Unseen Coaching
pitches.text: Players anticipate opponents perfectly while their shadows vanish at night. The shadows secretly win a parallel league, borrowing its victories and provoking opponents who will drag the school into darkness. Investigators learn the captain promised his shadow ownership of his body after graduation. They sever the stadium's midnight lighting connection, freeing the students but stranding their shadows in the other world. The team remains talented, now permanently shadowless and difficult to explain in yearbook photographs.

pitches.title: The Parents' Dream Team
pitches.text: Students win but forget friends and hobbies after each match. Parents' shared ambition has formed a psychic coach that removes interests unrelated to sport, with graduation completing their erasure. Investigators force the parents to witness a future of empty trophy-winning adults. Most withdraw their expectations, weakening the entity enough for the students to destroy it themselves. Abilities return to normal, and several children finally admit they never liked the sport, producing a much healthier but considerably smaller roster.

pitches.title: An Honest Cheater
pitches.text: A weak player knows every ball's destination while local accidents follow similar trajectories. A river oracle supplies certainty by displacing randomness onto bystanders. Investigators connect accidents to his prediction journal and make him destroy it before the final. He loses the promised scholarship along with the power, but the accidents reverse; the agency begins a fundraiser for tuition, realizing its usual assurance that someone higher up will provide resources is particularly cruel in this case.

pitches.title: Encore Forever
pitches.text: The band repeats its finale while spectators age between choruses. A dead fan's final wish traps the perfect concert, consuming real years to sustain it. Investigators find her partner refuses to leave because the ghost appears beside him in each chorus. He finally walks out during a deliberately imperfect song, breaking the wish and letting her depart. Some stolen years return, but his remain; he accepts the cost while the promoter advertises an unusually mature audience demographic.

pitches.title: Keep the Floor Alive
pitches.text: Anyone who stops dancing sees teeth under the floorboards. The drummer matched the rhythm keeping a buried devourer asleep, so silence would wake it. Investigators find its heart below the venue and sever it while performers maintain the beat, killing the creature before everyone collapses. The floor caves in but the crowd escapes; the drummer can no longer hear ordinary bass without panicking, and the club owner requests a positive statement about the evacuation's excellent audience engagement.

pitches.title: The Audience Is Missing
pitches.text: Performers cannot end because each sees a different audience invisible on camera. They are entertaining ghosts of passengers whose bus crashed before reaching this concert. Investigators recover the intended set list and help deliver the expected encore, finally completing the journey. Ghosts depart and trapped time releases the exhausted living crowd; the band discovers the original passengers were going to a different act and has to perform forty minutes of music it openly despises.

pitches.title: Contagious Rhythm
pitches.text: People dance without music and spread the compulsion by tapping feet. A melody is a sound creature's mating call, exhausting the town through endless courtship. Investigators find its answering species in an old field recording and play it through the speakers, drawing the creature into the recording equipment. They destroy the equipment before either sound escapes; the dancers recover, while the band's producer mourns losing what would unquestionably have been a commercially irresistible single.

pitches.title: The Headliner Isn't Here
pitches.text: The singer performs without breathing while backstage calls beg for rescue. Her voice sold itself to an applause spirit, leaving her trapped in the monitors as a double turns the crowd toward worship. Investigators reveal her imperfect unamplified singing from inside the speakers, breaking the double's hold. She escapes but never recovers her extraordinary voice, ending the concert with rough ordinary vocals; her manager calls this a catastrophe while her family recognizes her for the first time all night.

pitches.title: Dance Until Morning
pitches.text: The sky remains midnight outside as well as inside the concert. A sampled dawn ritual summoned the night goddess without its final dismissal, and the musicians cannot stop until she leaves. Investigators recover the missing verse and discover it requires one singer to accompany her beyond dawn. A technician volunteers, singing the world into morning before vanishing. The agency preserves his name and supports his family, whose compensation the promoter tries to classify as a charitable appearance fee.

pitches.title: The Last Quiet Person
pitches.text: A beat spreads through phones, compelling everyone except a deaf engineer to dance together. The musicians tapped a buried god that can incarnate only through unanimity. Investigators arrange competing rhythms directed by the immune engineer, disrupting synchronization and fracturing the god into harmless noise. The crowd recovers; reviewers describe the chaotic rescue as the worst finale they have heard, while the engineer quietly treasures being the only person whose professional judgment actually determined the set list.

pitches.title: Bodies for the Band
pitches.text: Collapsed dancers keep moving while musicians become younger. The band transfers exhaustion through a stolen spirit instrument, and the final chord will dump lethal fatigue on the audience. Investigators seize the instrument and reverse its strings, directing every stolen hour back to the musicians before breaking it. The crowd survives and the band ages past retirement, forced to admit its tireless image was exploitation; the rescue crew then discovers it too has worked thirty unpaid hours.

pitches.title: The Venue Demands More
pitches.text: New corridors route exiting guests back to the dance floor. The demolished club's ghost rebuilt itself around the show, afraid to vanish when the last customer leaves. Investigators offer remembrance elsewhere, but it refuses anything less than captivity. They lead guests through the buried original fire exit and burn its surviving sign, ending the ghost. The beloved venue disappears again, leaving rescued regulars to argue whether saving them justified destroying the last place they ever felt young.

pitches.title: Step Out of History
pitches.text: The dance floor slides through decades, collecting revelers after each chorus. A vintage record contains a time traveler's route home, but the band's improvisations have scrambled it. Investigators reconstruct the original melody from passengers' accounts, returning everyone to their own night. One musician chooses to remain in an earlier era where his sound is unprecedented; the rest return and discover his old records inspired their band, leaving his royalty dispute both genuine and impossible.

title: Weird french circus
description: The french circus is supposed to be weird, but is it supposed to be this weird?

pitches.title: The Missing Gravity Act
pitches.text: Acrobats float without ropes as spectators' belongings rise into the roof. Their captured gravity spirit is losing control, and the whole town will soon drift away. Investigators track fallen-star fragments in the costumes and break the binding that confines it. Gravity returns abruptly, injuring the team but saving the district; the circus loses its miraculous act, and its owner initially lists the investigators' hospital expenses under damage caused by unauthorized interference with equipment.

pitches.title: A Clown's True Face
pitches.text: A clown has a new face nightly, and spectators vanish from family photographs. He steals identities to assemble a human life, although his troupe already loves his monstrous self. Investigators show him their memories of that real friendship, convincing him to return the faces. Erased guests reappear; one refuses to relinquish the glamorous new identity the theft accidentally gave her, forcing the clown to live with a permanently missing piece of his own face.

pitches.title: The Animal-Free Menagerie
pitches.text: The circus advertises no captive animals, but performers roar inside their trunks. A sorcerer converted animals into people without asking, and stress is reversing the transformation. Investigators recover his spell and offer each performer a genuine choice. Some return to sanctuaries; others stay human, including the lion stage manager. The sorcerer tries to reverse everybody to recover ownership and is transformed into a rabbit, whose eventual caretaker takes consent substantially more seriously.

pitches.title: The Tent Outside Town
pitches.text: Visitors exit into unfamiliar cities as the ringmaster refuses to stop. The tent is a surviving fragment of a dream city, keeping itself real through captive audiences' wonder. Investigators find the central mast is its anchor and saw it down after locating the lost visitors. The city dissolves, leaving its residents stranded as new humans; they rebuild the troupe honestly, now performing to earn meals rather than to prevent their world from disappearing.

pitches.title: Applause for the Void
pitches.text: Acts remove rabbits, memories, then entire spectators from existence. The magician pays an emptiness god by passing real sacrifices off as illusions. Investigators locate missing people inside his shrinking hat and demonstrate the disappearances to the crowd, whose withdrawal of applause breaks the performance's consent. Everyone escapes except the magician, whose debt consumes him. His final bow remains visible as an empty outline onstage, receiving no further applause despite the promoter's persistent attempts.

pitches.title: The Strongman's Burden
pitches.text: The strongman's shoulders reveal streets and miniature people. He carries a compressed world whose keeper died, and increasingly elaborate acts secretly recruit a replacement. Investigators enter it and find its residents can stabilize their own sky only by demolishing their sacred palace. They expose the concealed machinery beneath it and organize the destruction, freeing the world from human support. The strongman quits delightedly, while the deposed miniature monarch demands compensation from an agency that cannot even pay normal-sized bills.

pitches.title: The Unfinished Finale
pitches.text: One performer dies in the same accident nightly and reappears each morning. A survivor trapped the troupe in its final show before a fire, changing details to save them without canceling her defining achievement. Investigators make her face the people repeatedly dying for that ambition and insist on evacuation instead. She abandons the perfect show, releasing the loop; everyone survives years older, and their first new finale is simply leaving the tent through correctly labeled exits.

pitches.title: Human Cannonball Return Address
pitches.text: Cannonball performers return as cheerful strangers while originals call from the clouds. The cannon opens a celestial migration route, allowing aliens to replace humans stranded in transit. Investigators hijack it to visit the detention station and recover the performers, but returning everyone overloads the cannon. They destroy the route after escape, stranding friendly aliens on Earth alongside the humans they impersonated; the circus hires them openly and struggles to separate their remarkably similar names on payroll.

pitches.title: The Taste of Wonder
pitches.text: Spectators lose surprise while candy floss grows living hair. A dying wonder-eater consumes more than spare excitement, stripping guests' capacity for awe. Investigators discover their counterfeit props can fool its appetite only temporarily, then lure it into a hall of recursive mirrors that offers endless apparent novelty. The guests recover as it remains trapped, neither cured nor starving; a guilty performer visits daily with genuinely new jokes, eventually exhausting the circus's entire repertoire.

pitches.title: The Mime's Prison
pitches.text: A mime's invisible walls trap real spectators. He learned gestures from a silent film that opened a demon's prison and has been containing the escaped creature one barrier at a time. Investigators reconstruct the reverse sequence, but completing it requires someone to remain inside. The mime sacrifices his freedom to seal the demon, leaving a harmless invisible box onstage. The troupe protects it forever, occasionally hearing muffled complaints when someone uses the prison as a coffee table.

pitches.title: The Costume Is Attending You
pitches.text: Cosplayers cannot remove their outfits and begin speaking their characters' dialogue involuntarily. A costume maker stitched cloth from a dream realm, letting fictional personalities borrow bodies, and the convention's grand finale will make the replacements permanent. Investigators find the maker hiding inside her own favorite heroine and cut the shared thread linking every outfit. Attendees recover, losing cherished costumes; the maker remains human and must face the ordinary audience reaction to her less miraculous work.

pitches.title: The Last Panel
pitches.text: A panel about a cult horror show attracts actors who died decades ago, and audience questions make their fictional murders happen in nearby rooms. A fan's obsessive reconstruction revived the program's murderous world, whose canceled finale never freed its characters. Investigators locate the unreleased script and perform its escape ending instead of the advertised reunion. The actors depart and the murders stop; the fan receives closure, then immediately complains that the improvised ending contradicted established continuity.

pitches.title: Special Guest from Nowhere
pitches.text: The convention's mysterious guest answers every fandom question perfectly but erases anyone who catches an error. It is a knowledge predator impersonating the promised celebrity, feeding on collective attention while organizers protect it to avoid refunding tickets. Investigators discover it cannot survive admitting uncertainty and stage contradictory questions derived from attendees' private experiences. Its persona collapses and captives return; organizers advertise the disastrous event as an intimate opportunity to see a beloved character break down.

pitches.title: The Dealer's Room
pitches.text: An autograph dealer sells signatures that grant buyers their idols' abilities while those idols weaken elsewhere. He found a pen that treats fame as a transferable substance and plans to auction an entire celebrity's life. Investigators trace a collapsing guest to the pen and force the dealer to sign his own name, giving away the identity anchoring every theft. Victims recover, and he becomes an anonymous nobody unable to prove ownership of his own lucrative business.

pitches.title: Convention in the Wrong Century
pitches.text: Attendees turn up in outfits from next year's releases, and the building exits onto a future ruined town. A science-fiction booth's authentic temporal prop has moved the con forward to its own advertised futuristic date. Investigators discover the future disaster began with a prop auction at this event and destroy the device rather than simply resetting it. The con returns, its future guests fading as their timeline vanishes; organizers still insist wristbands are nonrefundable.

pitches.title: Room Party for the Dead
pitches.text: Hotel guests hear a party inside a permanently vacant convention room, and living attendees return with deceased friends. The room hosts fans who died before meeting one another, borrowing living companions until they all feel included. Investigators locate its first guest's abandoned memorial and move the reunion there, allowing the dead company without abducting anyone. The room empties safely, but an investigator chooses to spend one last hour with a parent and emerges years older.

pitches.title: Exclusive Merchandise
pitches.text: A limited-edition figurine appears on every stall and grows whenever someone calls it rare. It is a status spirit fed by manufactured scarcity, turning collectors into display-ready miniatures as their obsession peaks. Investigators expose a warehouse full of identical stock and give the figures away until their exclusivity collapses. Captives regain size; the dealer loses his hoard, and the spirit survives as a cheap ubiquitous toy that now experiences embarrassment whenever anyone genuinely enjoys it.

pitches.title: The Convention Hive
pitches.text: Strangers at the con share memories and form impossibly coordinated queues. A communal fandom ritual awakened a group mind that plans to absorb the whole city into permanent togetherness. Investigators discover its first members secretly disagree on almost everything and amplify those suppressed arguments through the convention broadcast. The collective fractures, freeing attendees; friendships survive where they were real, while the organizers briefly consider marketing the actual psychic invasion as their most successful networking event.

pitches.title: Artists' Alley Exit
pitches.text: Artists sketch attendees who vanish into their drawings, while a quiet booth fills with portraits of frightened strangers. Its artist discovered a refuge from the real world and offers escape without explaining that paper bodies cannot leave. Investigators enter a portrait to rescue captives and find some prefer the refuge. They secure informed choices and destroy the artist's power to force entry; one investigator stays, leaving behind a flat smiling self-portrait and an utterly unusable emergency contact number.

pitches.title: The Badge Swap
pitches.text: Attendees wearing exchanged badges inherit one another's injuries, debts, and relatives. A masquerading trickster wants to demonstrate that human identity is merely a label, escalating the swap until nobody remembers their own lives. Investigators track the original badge printer and melt its enchanted plates, but identities can return only if people voluntarily admit who they are. Most recover; a wanted criminal refuses and remains someone else, leaving the team a solved phenomenon and a profoundly unresolved arrest.

title: Strange broadcast
description: A creepy broadcast is appearing on people’s TV screens

pitches.title: A Test of the Emergency System
pitches.text: A television broadcast warns of disasters seconds before they occur, persuading residents to obey increasingly dangerous instructions. A future survivor sends genuine warnings through a temporal antenna, but each avoided event shifts destruction elsewhere until he orders the town sacrificed to save his family. Investigators trace his changing landmarks and sever the antenna before compliance. They prevent the final disaster through ordinary evacuation, saving a different future while losing the only person who knew its precise dangers.

pitches.title: The Empty Presenter
pitches.text: A smiling presenter addresses viewers by name and gradually appears in reflections when screens are off. It is the abandoned personality of an old television host, fed by years of repeated footage until it can replace any lonely viewer. Investigators find the real retired host and broadcast their unglamorous present life, breaking the perfect persona's authority. Replaced viewers return; the host's honest complaints about arthritis unexpectedly gain a loyal audience the manufactured version could never keep.

pitches.title: Local News from Below
pitches.text: A station broadcasts reports of deaths before families have been notified, including one about a living investigator. The newsroom is a ghostly public service announcing souls stranded between life and death, and its report means the investigator is already dying unnoticed. The team tracks the reported scene and rescues them from a concealed carbon monoxide leak, then locates the other endangered subjects. The broadcast ends once its unfinished warnings reach people who can actually help.

pitches.title: Viewer Discretion
pitches.text: Anyone switching off a disturbing broadcast hears scratching inside the television. A predator uses viewing as a promise to watch its performance through completion, attacking those who break the bargain. Investigators decode a forgotten closing credit and film an ending where its fictional victim escapes, forcing the performance to finish. The creature loses access to viewers, but the final rescued household receives a permanently ruined television; its owner complains the agency solved the plot by spoiling the ending.

pitches.title: The Town's True Story
pitches.text: The broadcast reenacts private humiliations with dead relatives playing every part. A supernatural archivist believes complete public knowledge will heal the town, escalating to expose secrets that will destroy families. Investigators locate its original human subject, whose death followed the exposure of a private life, and demonstrate that disclosure is not automatically care. The archivist refuses, so they destroy its transmission vessel; truth already broadcast remains, forcing the town to live with consequences no exorcism can erase.

pitches.title: Please Stand By
pitches.text: Screens show a vacant waiting room where missing residents sit motionless. A signal from an unfinished afterlife terminal abducts anyone who falls asleep watching, mistakenly classifying sleep as death. Investigators enter through a camera feed and locate a faulty arrival bell, returning the living before processing begins. The dead passengers ask to come too, but the team cannot bring them back; the signal closes after genuine goodbyes, leaving the rescued viewers unusually willing to discuss their television habits.

pitches.title: The Commercial Break
pitches.text: A sinister commercial offers ordinary products that appear instantly, each followed by a stranger's disappearance. An alien trader interprets consumer attention as permission to exchange equivalent living material for goods. Investigators reconstruct the trade language and demand reversals, then disable the transmitter before the broadcaster can appeal. Missing people return, but the team must surrender every received product, including a miracle cure; its recipient survives only through ordinary emergency treatment and an exceptionally costly hospital stay.

pitches.title: Pirate Signal
pitches.text: The broadcast shows a panicked crew begging viewers to steer a ship visible in the night sky. It comes from a vessel crossing dream space, where audience belief supplies navigation but an unseen passenger twists instructions toward Earth. Investigators spot the passenger only in delayed recordings and guide the crew to eject it into empty dream space. The vessel escapes, while the trapped creature continues pleading from broken screens; the agency learns to store evidence unplugged.

pitches.title: The Smile Channel
pitches.text: A cheerful children's broadcast makes adults smile uncontrollably while their sadness appears as monsters outside. Its host is a grief-eating spirit whose attempt to help excludes emotions it cannot digest. Investigators expose the creatures as expelled human sorrow and interrupt the program with honest accounts of loss, returning emotions to their owners. The spirit retreats, and viewers recover; one investigator misses the temporary happiness enough to keep a recording, an unresolved temptation disguised as evidence retention.

pitches.title: Already Recorded
pitches.text: The creepy broadcast shows investigators searching a house, then dying there, although they have not accepted the case. It is footage from a timeline where their destroyed parent agency tried to contain a reality predator. They use details of their predicted failure to bait the predator into the broadcasting machine and destroy it, preventing that ending. The final clip shows their agency's last real experts making the same desperate call for nonexistent backup, ending the team's comforting belief that help is delayed.

title: Strange photographs
description: A collection of photographs has been discovered which deserves attention

pitches.title: The Person Between Us
pitches.text: Group photographs contain a stranger who moves closer to the camera in later prints. The figure is a friendship parasite inserted into remembered outings, and the owner already recalls lending it a house key. Investigators compare negatives with independent diaries, exposing moments nobody actually shared with it. Destroying the altered prints expels it from memory, but one investigator retains a genuine affection the creature cultivated; the restored group can no longer quite agree who belongs in its replacement photograph.

pitches.title: The Last Good Summer
pitches.text: Photographs show a vanished lakeside town enjoying one perfect day while their subjects age in newer prints. A photographer trapped residents inside images to protect them from a flood, but his death ended the maintenance keeping their world alive. Investigators enter the original negative and lead survivors out before it fades. They return decades late, grieving lost relatives but alive; the town's replacement resort offers complimentary refreshments instead of acknowledging it was built over their homes.

pitches.title: Evidence of Tomorrow
pitches.text: A collection depicts future deaths with a camera visible in each reflection. Investigators discover the camera does not predict murder: photographing someone creates the fatal sequence necessary to reproduce its picture. Its frightened owner has been taking more images to find a way to save the subjects.
