The team exposes the causal loop and destroys the lens before its final image develops, stopping the deaths; the saved people still remember their dying moments whenever someone asks them to smile.

pitches.title: Missing from the Negative
pitches.text: Family photographs lose one person each night while everyone insists the frames were always arranged that way. The original photographer used soul-sensitive film, and a developing chemical is now dissolving the preserved identities. Investigators follow surviving handwritten captions to retrieve the people as translucent figures and wash the negatives before their last outlines vanish. Most return; an unlabeled infant cannot be identified in time, leaving a restored family grieving a loss they can no longer fully remember.

pitches.title: The Vacation Nobody Took
pitches.text: An estate collection shows locals holidaying on a beautiful island none remember visiting. A dream travel service once sold genuine journeys while keeping customers' sleeping bodies, and the island has begun billing overdue guests by abducting their descendants. Investigators locate the surviving operator and destroy the old soul ledger, freeing the debtors. The resort vanishes, but one photograph proves an investigator's parents met there; they accept the mystery without risking their existence to demand a refund.

pitches.title: The Photographer's Blind Spot
pitches.text: Every image contains a distorted empty patch, and rooms matching the photographs now develop the same absence. The photographer documented a creature nobody could consciously see, giving its otherwise unreal body a stable footprint in reality. Investigators map the patches and burn the complete sequence in reverse order, unraveling its foothold before it occupies the town. The creature disappears with the photographer's lost memories; her family keeps one harmless blurred portrait instead of demanding the miraculous archive back.

pitches.title: Proof of a Happy Ending
pitches.text: Photographs show grieving families reunited with dead relatives who begin knocking on doors. A camera reconstructs whatever its subjects wish to remember, producing doubles that know only idealized histories and punish anyone who contradicts them. Investigators find the original death records and make each family confront the imperfect people they actually loved, dissolving the dangerous idealizations. The dead remain dead; several households recover relationships with living relatives they had neglected while waiting for impossible restoration.

pitches.title: The Other Side of the Portrait
pitches.text: Turning portraits over reveals living people begging from miniature rooms. A portraitist traded clients' unwanted traits to a mirror collector, who gradually claimed whole identities instead. Investigators track the collector through the studio's self-portrait and exchange its own image for its prisoners, binding it inside the frame. People return with their supposedly undesirable qualities intact; the portraitist loses the magical power that made every client look charming and finally has to learn lighting.

pitches.title: The Camera at the Disaster
pitches.text: Photographs reveal unseen hands saving people during historic disasters, including one belonging to an investigator. They are images of a rescue relay across time, and examining them summons the next rescuer into the pictured catastrophe. The team follows the sequence willingly, saving strangers until it reaches the disaster that destroyed the parent agency. They cannot prevent that loss without breaking every earlier rescue, so preserve the relay and return knowing exactly why nobody will answer their support calls.

pitches.title: All the Dogs Remember
pitches.text: The photographs show the same dog beside unrelated families across a century, and examining one brings it to the door. It is a guardian spirit that follows descendants of a child it once failed to save, and the collection is warning that a final descendant is in danger. Investigators trace the family and prevent the accident alongside the dog, completing its promise. It becomes mortal and stays with the rescued child; the team counts a normal veterinarian bill as unusually welcome evidence.

title: Supporting school club
description: An after school club dedicated to the paranormal

pitches.title: The Club Knows More
pitches.text: The after-school club asks for official sponsorship after capturing a creature the agency cannot identify. Their immaculate research reveals it is a larval apocalypse, contained through months of unpaid work while their supposed adult experts supplied empty assurances. Investigators admit the agency's limits and help the students destroy its anchor before hatching. The club saves town but refuses further sponsorship, establishing a genuinely transparent support network; the adults earn only a carefully supervised place on its volunteer roster.

pitches.title: Summoning a Friend
pitches.text: Club members perform rituals that attract increasingly dangerous visitors, insisting they are searching for a missing classmate. Her imaginary friend became real when the club collectively believed in it, then hid her inside its invented world to keep her from growing up. Investigators enter through her childhood notebook and help her choose change over eternal friendship. She escapes, and the being collapses into a drawing; the club keeps the notebook without ever again using belief as a substitute for consent.

pitches.title: The Unhaunted School
pitches.text: The club begs for a haunting investigation although the school looks perfectly ordinary. It has been training a ghost to remove bullying by deleting victims from everybody's memories, and the club's missing founder is the first erased student. Investigators follow anonymous yearbook gaps into a room of forgotten children and destroy the school's original memorial bell, the ghost's anchor. Everyone returns to a world that still contains cruelty, leaving adults with work they can no longer outsource to the paranormal.

pitches.title: Independent Research
pitches.text: Students proudly present a demon trapped in a lunch box that grants small favors. They think adults are overreacting because it is polite and its gifts have no obvious price. Investigators uncover a missing day from every child's memory: the demon receives time during which it can act through them. They destroy the box during its next collection, expelling it but exposing crimes committed in borrowed bodies; the club needs protection and honest restitution rather than a triumphant certificate.

pitches.title: The Club's Oldest Member
pitches.text: A school club photograph from 1931 includes its current teenage president. He is immortal because a spirit accepted his childhood promise never to abandon the club, replacing graduating friends for generations. Investigators find the original promise and help current students formally continue the club without him. Freed, he ages naturally to his true years but lives long enough for a real retirement; his final meeting consists of handing over keys instead of making another farewell seem temporary.

pitches.title: Field Trip Beyond the Fence
pitches.text: Students find a shortcut to a graveyard that never appears on maps and invite investigators to prove it safe. It is a school for ghosts whose teacher is recruiting living pupils to replace students who have crossed over. The team discovers enrollment becomes permanent when the visitors answer roll call and disrupts the ceremony by calling their real living names. Everyone escapes, but the route closes on the ghost teacher's desperate plea; the club starts maintaining the neglected graves without attending class.

pitches.title: The Wrong Mentor
pitches.text: The club receives polished video lessons from the supposedly expert agency, teaching rituals that actually weaken local reality. The sender is a surviving parasite wearing the destroyed organization's training archives, cultivating obedient new hosts. Investigators recognize an old official's impossible continued appearance and expose the source, but the students initially trust the professional videos over their scruffy rescuers. A failed lesson finally proves the danger, and together they burn the archive; genuine knowledge is lost alongside the threat.

pitches.title: Election of the Moon King
pitches.text: A joke election makes the paranormal club president's commands affect the sky. The students accidentally used an authentic lunar succession ritual, and rival spirits arrive to kill the new monarch before the next eclipse. Investigators uncover the abdication rite, which requires freely surrendering every granted power. The president relinquishes them despite pressure to use them against bullies, ending the contest; the club elects a new leader using ordinary paper, and the former king finds anonymity unexpectedly restful.

pitches.title: A Club of One
pitches.text: The paranormal club's attendance list has twelve students, but investigators can find only its lonely founder. He created companions through an occult exercise, and they are stealing real classmates' lives to survive graduation. The team confronts the companions with their dependence and offers a choice between release and killing the people they imitate. Most fade willingly; one attacks and must be destroyed. The founder survives grieving, then starts attending a real club where friendship develops slowly and cannot be conjured on demand.

pitches.title: The Students Who Stayed Late
pitches.text: The club remains at school after closing and returns home with identical false memories. They have been helping a damaged dimensional visitor rebuild its craft, paying for parts with sleep it harvests from them. Investigators find their real memories in its engine and seize them, grounding the craft. The visitor admits it cannot go home without hurting them, so the team destroys the engine and helps it adapt to Earth; the students gain an alien friend who finally contributes something besides homework excuses.

title: Strange screenings
description: The local movie festival includes some disturbing entries

pitches.title: The Audience Cut
pitches.text: A festival film shows its own audience, killing a different viewer in each screening and leaving their seat empty afterward. The director filmed a death spirit that thinks editing human life is artistic improvement. Investigators recover earlier cuts and discover discarded victims alive between frames, then splice an ending where the director destroys his camera. The spirit must follow its completed narrative, freeing everyone; the director survives but can never again see moving images without appearing briefly in the background.

pitches.title: A Documentary of Nowhere
pitches.text: A disturbing documentary follows residents of a town absent from maps, and festivalgoers begin remembering homes there. The town was erased by a failed agency containment operation, surviving only on film and borrowing identities to become real. Investigators recover evidence of its actual population and screen that truth instead of letting it steal people. Survivors reappear, displaced and angry; the festival's celebratory humanitarian branding receives a blunt response from people who need housing rather than a standing ovation.

pitches.title: The Monster Is the Critic
pitches.text: Festival critics vanish after harsh reviews, and the director blames an overzealous fan. His practical-effects monster was built from living occult material and believes reviews of the film are judgments of its worth as a person. Investigators discover it stores critics inside its body, forcing them to watch endlessly. They free the captives and destroy its animating heart after it refuses to stop; the director's film gains notoriety, which the survivors resent more than its original bad ending.

pitches.title: The Lost Childhood Film
pitches.text: A restored children's film makes adults regress physically while remembering a terrifying missing scene. Its creator trapped his dying child inside the film and feeds her new childhoods to keep her alive. Investigators enter the projection and let the girl learn what her survival costs, prompting her to end her father's bargain. Adults return to age as she finally dies; the team saves one ordinary home movie for her father, who now must mourn without a captive audience.

pitches.title: The Festival Jury
pitches.text: A screening invites viewers to vote on a character's fate, and strangers elsewhere experience the selected events. The film is a supernatural trial assembled by a vindictive medium who disguises real defendants as fictional villains. Investigators connect locations to missing people and interrupt the vote, projecting evidence the medium edited away. The audience overturns the convictions, restoring victims; the medium becomes his own final defendant and must face a verdict without controlling the script.

pitches.title: Subtitles for the Dead
pitches.text: Foreign films acquire subtitles in viewers' native languages that ask for help, while spoken dialogue remains ordinary. Ghosts caught in the cinema's old fire communicate through captions, but the festival's restoration project will erase their last outlet. Investigators trace the pleas to an unreported locked exit and reveal the owner's culpability, letting the ghosts leave after acknowledgment. The subtitles disappear; the restored films remain, now screened beside an uncomfortable statement the current owner cannot market away.

pitches.title: A Film That Dreams You
pitches.text: Audiences wake after the screening with memories of lives they never led, and their actual days start resembling the plot. The film is an alien dream organism growing human experiences inside its viewers to complete its first story. Investigators expose its dependence on a single coherent ending and improvise contradictory live finales, fragmenting the invasion. Everyone regains control, though borrowed memories remain; an investigator uses an imaginary marriage's lessons to finally end their very real disastrous relationship.

pitches.title: The Director's Final Draft
pitches.text: A festival film shows scenes from the team's lives filmed at angles no camera could reach. Its dead director edits reality toward a perfect climax, repeatedly resurrecting investigators only to kill them more dramatically. They discover the editing room hidden inside the reel and destroy it, breaking his control. The last resurrection does not repeat, leaving one colleague dead; the survivors rescue the audience without a neat finale and decline the festival's request for a recorded reaction shot.

pitches.title: Sell-Out Screening
pitches.text: A tiny experimental film sells out, yet surveillance shows many patrons arriving with no faces. They are dream creatures using the festival's shared darkness to borrow human form, planning to leave inside spectators at the final applause. Investigators turn on the lights before the ending and project the creatures' real bodies from the original footage, breaking the camouflage. Most flee back into film; one harmless refugee receives voluntary shelter, while the organizers are appalled by the apparent audience drop-off.

pitches.title: The Missing Final Reel
pitches.text: Every disturbing entry ends before resolution, and viewers compulsively reenact scenes around town seeking closure. The reels were severed from films that contain their fictional worlds, releasing characters who now commandeer human lives to finish their stories. Investigators retrieve the stolen endings from a collector and screen them together, returning most characters home. One ending demands a genuine human death, so they burn that film instead; its homeless hero survives as an ordinary person furious about losing his destined triumph.
